clue.text: Bread container for actor, b. '28

parts.note: a cob is a round loaf of bread
an urn is a vessel or container

explanation.surface: A breadbin is offered up as a prop for an old film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble 'Class of '28' ties the themed clues to people born or died in 1928; James Coburn, star of The Magnificent Seven, was born then.
explanation.definitionFit: James Coburn was an American film actor born in 1928, matching the birth-year theme.

clue.text: Document that's written in prison for linguistic philosopher b. '28

indicators.note: written in means set down inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: choky is British slang for prison
MS is short for manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: A philosopher pens a paper while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Noam Chomsky, born 1928, is a linguist and philosopher famous for generative grammar.

clue.text: One taking month to run up, tailor's first suit

indicators.note: in a down clue, run up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Feb is February abbreviated

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of tailor

explanation.surface: A tailor takes a month to run up a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run up' sounds like tailoring but reverses I FEB. 'Suit' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit something is to suit it, to be fitting for it.

clue.text: Shot, if parried, delivered as a continuous stream

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A fencer's shot, parried, sets off a flurry of thrusts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid-fire describes questions or shots coming in quick succession, a stream.

clue.text: A dry, barren, endless essay

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. dry, drinking no alcohol

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the barren word is lopped off

parts.note: empty means barren or bare

explanation.surface: A dull, sterile piece of writing that drags on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a noun for a piece of writing but means a try.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to try, and an essay can be a noun for a try or effort.

clue.text: Guardian published shortly for writer and poet, b. '28

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over one

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last letter from the published word

parts.note: a book that is out is published

explanation.surface: The Guardian newspaper is to print a poet's work soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper that runs this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Maya Angelou, born 1928, wrote I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings and much poetry.

clue.text: Emperor keeping sixth of treasure in chest, commonly?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one letter is kept inside

parts.note: tits is common slang for breasts, hence a chest

indicators.note: sixth of picks the sixth letter of treasure

explanation.surface: An emperor guards treasure in a chest, as the vulgar would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks like a treasure box but is slang for a bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Sociobiologist, b.'28 cut above solid figure for composer, b. '28

indicators.note: in a down clue, above puts the first piece over the second
cut trims the last letter of the surname

parts.note: Desmond Morris, author of The Naked Ape, was born in 1928
a cone is a solid geometric figure

explanation.surface: One 1928 birth is set against another, a scientist trimmed atop a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennio Morricone, born 1928, composed film scores such as The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.

clue.text: Vulnerable spot for actor, b. '28

definitions.meaning: the side of the head, where a blow is dangerous

explanation.surface: An actor's weak spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple is a thin-skulled area of the head; Shirley Temple was a famous child actress.

clue.text: Approximately dropping 20%, American company performing

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a piece of the approximate word is shed

parts.note: circa means approximately
a fifth of the five-letter word for approximately is one letter, here its last

explanation.surface: An American company sheds about a fifth of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping 20%' sounds like business news but removes one letter of five.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus is a travelling troupe of performers.

clue.text: Mouldy hop seed

parts.note: food that has gone mouldy is off
a spring is a hop or leap

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a hop seed that has gone mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hop' looks like the plant, but it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed can mean descendants or progeny, as in the biblical 'seed of Abraham'.

clue.text: Buzz Lightyear's back in hit, briefly

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
briefly means the hitting word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to thump is to hit

indicators.note: back points to the final letter of the name Lightyear

explanation.surface: Buzz Lightyear, the Toy Story spaceman, is struck by a quick blow to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' looks like part of the cartoon name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a low continuous humming sound, a kind of buzz.

clue.text: Boss of weekend issue, stuffed?

parts.note: the Saturday edition of a paper, abbreviated Sat
ED, short for editor, is the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: The editor of the weekend paper is perhaps overfed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated means full to satisfaction, so stuffed with food.

clue.text: Heavenly performance of a cellist inspires ecstasy

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, taking a letter inside
a performance of the phrase 'a cellist' plays its letters in a new order

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cellist's heavenly playing transports the listener to rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance of' turns A CELLIST into CELSTIAL, and E goes inside it after CEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means belonging to the sky or heaven, so heavenly.

clue.text: Fine dishes for privileged youngsters

parts.note: yup, an informal yes, says that's fine
pies are baked dishes

explanation.surface: Rich young things are served posh food.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuppies are young urban professionals, affluent young people of the 1980s.

clue.text: First coming down close to bottom, smack proved painful for political activist, d. '28

indicators.text: First coming down close to bottom
indicators.note: the first letter drops down the column to sit just above the last

parts.note: to spank is to smack
hurt means proved painful

explanation.surface: A smack on the bottom proves painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First coming down close to bottom' takes S from the top of SPANKHURT and sets it before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst, leader of the British suffragettes, died in 1928.

clue.text: End broken off round nuts, securing instant release

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is clasped inside the other
nuts means crazy, so the remaining letters go mad and rearrange
says the last letter of the word round is snapped away

parts.note: taken as written
MO, short for moment, is an instant

explanation.surface: A mechanic snaps off a bolt's end and frees it quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End broken off' leaves ROUN and 'nuts' scrambles it; 'securing' then holds the instant inside. 'Nuts' looks like the bolts' partners but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmoor a boat is to release it from its moorings.

clue.text: Home of brothers for comedian, b. '28

definitions.meaning: a monastery, where monks live together as brothers
Bob ..., British comic and game-show host, born 1928

explanation.surface: A comedian lives where friars do.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery houses brother monks; Bob Monkhouse was a British comedian born in 1928.

clue.text: Where hammer found nailing lid on gradually, working effectively

indicators.note: nailing means pinning down, holding a letter fixed inside

parts.note: the hammer, or malleus, is a small bone in the ear

indicators.note: the lid on a word is its top, i.e. first letter

explanation.surface: A carpenter slowly nails down a lid with a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: The hammer is not a tool here but the bone in the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in gear has its gears engaged, so it is running properly.

clue.text: Control a thoroughfare, unchecked

parts.note: to run a business is to control it
a way is a road or thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Traffic police try to control a road that has gone unregulated.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway horse or process is out of control, unchecked.

clue.text: Long time sitting on stool in lower chamber

indicators.note: sitting on places the long time next to the stool, the stool coming first

parts.note: stool is excrement, i.e. dung
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: Someone sits on a stool for ages in the lower house of a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower chamber' looks political but means a cellar prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell, a chamber below a castle.

clue.text: One of 28 played for pianist, b. '28

definitions.meaning: a standard double-six set has 28 tiles
Fats ..., rock and roll pianist, born 1928

explanation.surface: A pianist plays one of 28 pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a tile from a 28-piece set; Fats Domino was a New Orleans pianist.

clue.text: Effortlessly talented, score mark?

definitions.meaning: a sign in a musical score cancelling a sharp or flat

explanation.surface: A gifted pupil marks a test score.
explanation.definitionFit: A born talent is a natural, and the natural sign in music restores a note to its plain pitch.

clue.text: Military leave for artist, b. '28

parts.note: war, as in war service, is military activity
hol is short for holiday, leave from work

explanation.surface: An artist is granted army leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol, the pop artist behind the soup-can prints, was born in 1928.

clue.text: Personal style I had with memo inscribed with name

indicators.note: inscribed with says a letter is written into the middle of the other letters
to style is to fashion or shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes the personal style of a memo carrying their name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' anagrams I HAD MEMO; 'inscribed with' sets N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem argument attacks the person rather than the point, so it is personal.

clue.text: Perhaps sentence by a magistrate holds up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upwards
holds means contains, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A magistrate's sentence is delayed, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' points to EBYAM inside 'sentence by a magistrate'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are synonyms expressing possibility.

clue.text: Pick up end of carpet beater

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of carpet

explanation.surface: Someone collects a carpet beater, used for thrashing dust from rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beater' seems tied to the carpet, but it is the organ that beats.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart beats steadily, so it is a beater in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Wood shaving now shaved?

indicators.note: shaving takes off the top, removing the first letter

parts.note: a man who is now shaved is balder than before

explanation.surface: A woodworker shaves a plank and shavings fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaving' looks like woodwork but trims a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alder is a tree of the birch family, and its timber is a wood.

clue.text: Only just missing line for writer, d. '28

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: hardly means only just, barely

explanation.surface: A writer barely misses a line in the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy, the novelist and poet of Wessex, died in 1928.

clue.text: Wine, fruit and fresh rolls failed in business

indicators.note: rolls means turns over, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: red is wine
a nut is a fruit
new means fresh

explanation.surface: A deli selling wine, fruit and fresh bread rolls goes bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like bread but signals reading the whole string backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that went under collapsed, i.e. went bankrupt or failed.

clue.text: Draw tail of animal like an aquatic carnivore?

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: ottery is a playful made-up adjective, 'like an otter'

explanation.surface: An artist sketches an otter's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word OTTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw, prizes going to tickets picked at random.

clue.text: Detailing favourite part, engine driver?

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: detailing is read as de-tailing, removing a word's tail letter

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: An actor details a favourite role playing a train driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engine driver' is not a railwayman but what drives an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is fuel that powers a car's engine, so cryptically it drives one.
